actor: Hosted-API model lifecycle product manager, DeepSeek platform
job: Deciding how V4-Flash checkpoints are addressed after the 0731 build replaced the preview behind the unchanged deepseek-v4-flash name.
outcome: A second, version-identified V4-Flash model id in the API model list, served alongside the floating name with no announced shutdown date.
motivation: Customers who qualified the preview now hold sign-offs their API key cannot reach, and a pinned id is the cheapest answer.

task.what: Specify a two-address scheme for V4-Flash
task.where: DeepSeek platform roadmap and model-naming design review
task.why: A single address hides checkpoint substitution from paying callers
task.how: Dated immutable id strings mapped to one frozen checkpoint

actor: API gateway and model-routing engineer, DeepSeek serving platform
job: Building the binding that resolves a model string to a checkpoint, today one floating name that silently re-based callers onto the 0731 build.
outcome: Routing that holds one string immutable against a named checkpoint while the floating name keeps advancing, both live on the same endpoint.
motivation: Without a routing layer addressing two checkpoints at once, the decision to publish a pinned id has nothing to ship on.

task.who: DeepSeek API gateway, model registry and request-routing engineers
task.what: Bind an immutable model string to one checkpoint
task.where: DeepSeek model registry and request-routing layer
task.why: The floating name cannot also promise a fixed build
task.how: Model registry entries keyed to checkpoint digests, not aliases

actor: Inference serving and fleet capacity engineer, DeepSeek hosted platform
job: Planning how long the superseded V4-Flash preview weights stay resident and routable on serving hardware now carrying the re-tuned 0731 checkpoint.
outcome: An older checkpoint kept warm and addressable, so a version-identified id has something to serve rather than pointing at a retired build.
motivation: If the earlier build stops being served entirely, no second address can exist and the two-address scheme fails on capacity alone.

task.who: DeepSeek inference infrastructure and serving capacity planning staff
task.what: Reserve capacity for a superseded V4-Flash checkpoint
task.where: DeepSeek inference fleet capacity and retirement planning
task.why: A pinned id needs live weights behind it
task.how: Checkpoint residency budgets weighed against current-model serving demand

outcome: A pinned V4-Flash id offered at the existing rate card, removing the pricing objection that would otherwise keep it unpublished.
motivation: Holding the price flat across a better checkpoint spent the lever for charging for a pin, leaving publication as the cheapest concession.

task.what: Price a frozen-checkpoint address against current rates
task.where: DeepSeek rate card and margin review for hosted inference
task.why: A free pin retains buyers a re-price would lose
task.how: Margin models comparing pinned-route cost to churn exposure

motivation: Documentation, not a release note, is what a buyer's change-control process can cite when it needs tomorrow to return what today returned.

task.where: DeepSeek API model list and pricing documentation pages
